Bug_Title: DLS: Dead store of class literal (DLS_DEAD_STORE_OF_CLASS_LITERAL)
Bug_Details:
This instruction assigns a class literal to a variable and then never uses it.
The behavior of this differs in Java 1.4 and in Java 5.
In Java 1.4 and earlier, a reference to Foo.class would force the static initializer
for Foo to be executed, if it has not been executed already.
In Java 5 and later, it does not.
 See Oracle's article on Java SE compatibility
for more details and examples, and suggestions on how to force class initialization in Java 5+.
 Foo.class Foo
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by assigning the class literal Foo.class to the variable unusedClass and then never using it. This assignment does not trigger the static initializer of the Foo class in Java 5 and later, which is the intended demonstration of the bug.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method. Since the showBug method returns null, the assertNotNull assertion fails, demonstrating the dead store of the class literal.
